passage: All day at school Preeti ran her lines: raise the eyebrows when Tanya talks, say "No way!" at the right pause, laugh a beat after the others. She had written them in the back of her rough book. By the time the auto dropped her at the colony gate, her jaw ached. Inside, she didn't say hello. She dropped her bag, lay on the cool floor under the dining table and pulled her dupatta over her face. Nirmala, her mother, came from the kitchen, saw her, and asked nothing. She switched off the tube light, stopped the mixer halfway through the chutney and set a glass of water by Preeti's hand. An hour later a small voice came from under the table. "Mummy, can I just be weird this evening?" "Be exactly you," Nirmala said.

qa.q: Where had Preeti written her lines?
qa.a: In the back of her rough book.

qa.q: How did Preeti feel by the time she got home, and what shows it?
qa.a: She was drained and overwhelmed; her jaw ached, she didn't say hello, and she lay under the table with her dupatta over her face.

qa.q: Which choices by Nirmala gave Preeti a place to rest?
qa.a: She asked nothing, switched off the light, stopped the noisy mixer and left water nearby, then told Preeti to be exactly herself.

qa.q: How might the evening have gone if Nirmala had demanded to know what was wrong?
qa.a: Preeti might have shut down further or broken down, because she had no energy left to explain.

grounding: It shows a teenager who scripts expressions to fit in at school and shuts down at home, where acceptance lets her rest.

passage: "You were great at the fest, man. Everyone laughed at your jokes." "They weren't my jokes, Hemant. I practised them from a video. Forty times." "Seriously?" "And I watched how Rishi laughs and copied the timing. Head back, two seconds." "Why would you do that?" "Because when I laugh my way, people stare." Farhan pulls his hood over his eyes. "I've got nothing left. My face hurts from making faces." Ammi's voice from the doorway: "Farhan, the room's dark, the fan's on low. No dinner talk tonight unless you want it." "Thanks, Ammi." "Should I go?" Hemant asks. "Stay. Just don't need me to talk." "Fine by me. I'll read. And you don't have to do the Rishi laugh here." A snort comes from under the hood: Farhan's own laugh, crooked and short.

qa.q: How many times did Farhan practise the jokes?
qa.a: Forty times.

qa.q: Why does Farhan copy Rishi's laugh?
qa.a: He is afraid of being stared at, because when he laughs his own way, people stare.

qa.q: What choice helped Farhan rest after the fest?
qa.a: Ammi kept the room dark and quiet with no dinner talk, and Hemant stayed without needing him to talk.

qa.q: What is it like for Hemant to learn the jokes were practised?
qa.a: Hemant is surprised, since the fest looked easy for Farhan, but then understands and offers him a place to be himself.

grounding: It shows a teenager who copies peers' scripts and laughs to fit in and is exhausted afterward, with acceptance at home giving him rest.

passage: Looking back at ninth grade, I can see how hard I worked just to seem normal. I studied the way Arohi laughed at lunch and copied the timing. I practised faces in the bathroom mirror: surprised, interested, bored. I had lines ready for every conversation, like "same, yaar" and "no way." Everybody said I was fun. Then I'd get home and could not speak at all. I'd lie on the floor of my room in the dark, and sometimes I cried for no reason I could name. My mother would put a glass of water by the door and say, "No questions today, Joseph." That door was the first place I could stop acting. I think it saved that whole year.

qa.q: Where did Joseph practise faces?
qa.a: Joseph practised faces in the bathroom mirror: surprised, interested, bored.

qa.q: How did Joseph feel after school, and what shows it?
qa.a: Joseph felt completely drained and exhausted from acting, unable to speak and lying on the floor in the dark, sometimes crying.

qa.q: Why did the mother's approach help?
qa.a: Joseph's mother left water and asked no questions, so home became a place where Joseph could rest without having to perform.

qa.q: How might Arohi see Joseph at lunch?
qa.a: Arohi probably saw Joseph as fun and easy company, without knowing how much effort the copied laughter took.

grounding: Shows a teenager who copies peers' expressions and uses scripts to fit in, then shuts down at home, where acceptance gives rest.

passage:
Note for the school counsellor, from Anand's mother, Himani.
Anand, fifteen, comes home from school every day looking cheerful at the gate. His teachers say he jokes with everyone. But the moment he is inside he drops his bag, sits on the floor and rocks, sometimes for an hour. If I ask even one question, he shouts or goes silent. Yesterday he said, "I copy what the others do all day. I'm so tired of being someone else." I have set up a corner with a mat and dim light where no one talks to him until dinner. Could the school give him a quiet place at lunch too? I would like to meet you this week.

qa.q: How long does Anand sometimes rock after coming home?
qa.a: He sometimes rocks for an hour.

qa.q: How does Anand feel about copying others all day?
qa.a: He feels deeply tired and worn out by pretending, saying he is so tired of being someone else.

qa.q: What did Himani do next that could help Anand?
qa.a: She set up a quiet corner at home where no one talks to him until dinner, and asked the counsellor for a quiet place at lunch and a meeting.

qa.q: How might the school counsellor see Anand after reading this note?
qa.a: The counsellor may realise that the cheerful boy at school is using a lot of energy to fit in, and look for ways to lower that strain.

grounding: Shows a teenager who copies peers to fit in and then shuts down at home, where acceptance and a quiet space let him rest.

passage:
Friday night.
Class party today. I had my lines ready: "Nice shirt." "Haha, true." I copied Tejas every time he laughed, a half-second late. I kept my face moving. Nobody noticed anything. I think I did it perfectly.
In the auto home my hands started shaking. At home I couldn't answer when Papa asked about dinner. I went into my room and sat inside the cupboard with the door half shut. Everything was too loud, even the fan.
Papa didn't push. He left a cup of tea on the desk and said through the door, "I'm just outside if you want." That's all.
I came out at ten. We watched cricket without talking. It was the first easy hour all day.
Saurabh

qa.q: Where did Saurabh sit after coming home?
qa.a: Saurabh sat inside the cupboard with the door half shut.

qa.q: How did Saurabh feel after the party, and what are the signs?
qa.a: Saurabh felt exhausted and overwhelmed; hands shook in the auto, answering Papa was impossible and even the fan felt too loud.

qa.q: What did Papa get right after Saurabh came home?
qa.a: He did not push or ask questions; he left tea and said he was just outside, which gave Saurabh room to rest.

qa.q: What was the party like for Tejas, compared with Saurabh?
qa.a: Tejas was probably just enjoying himself, unaware that Saurabh was copying his laughs and working hard all evening.

grounding: Shows a teenager using copied laughs and scripts to fit in, then shutting down at home, where a parent's acceptance offers rest.

passage:
Neelam: Didi, are you home?
Ishita: Yes, in the kitchen. How was school?
Neelam: I did Riya's laugh all day. Practised the "haha omg" face in the mirror at lunch.
Neelam: Said "same" to everything.
Ishita: That sounds tiring.
Neelam: I'm SO tired. I'm going to come home and I can't talk. Please don't ask me anything. Please.
Ishita: Okay. Your room is dark, fan's on, headphones are on the bed. No questions till you're ready.
Neelam: Mummy will ask about the test.
Ishita: I'll tell her later. You don't have to perform here.
Neelam: Thank you.
Neelam: Can we just watch the train videos after dinner? Without talking?
Ishita: Yes. Silent train videos. Our thing.

qa.q: What did Neelam practise in the mirror at lunch?
qa.a: The "haha omg" face.

qa.q: How is Neelam feeling on the way home?
qa.a: Neelam feels completely exhausted and anxious about being asked to talk after a whole day of copying others to fit in.

qa.q: What did Ishita do that could help anyone in Neelam's place?
qa.a: She prepared a quiet, dark room, kept questions away and made home a place where Neelam doesn't have to perform.

qa.q: If you were Ishita, what might you want Neelam to know?
qa.a: That it is safe to be natural at home, and that loving Neelam doesn't depend on the laughs and faces used at school.

grounding: Neelam masks at school by copying a friend's expressions and scripts, arrives home exhausted, and her sister's acceptance gives a place to rest.
